newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Housing and fuel drive Dec South African inflation.
newsitem.headline: Housing and fuel drive Dec South African inflation.

text.p: Higher housing and fuel costs were the main drivers behind South African inflation in December 1996, the Central Statistcal Service said on Tuesday.
The consumer price index rose 1.0 percent in December from November after rising 0.4 percent in November, while the year-on-year rise was 9.4 percent versus November's 9.2 percent.
The data was broadly in line with analysts' expectations and South African bonds showed little immediate response to the data.

Housing contributed 0.4 of a percentage point to to the 1.0 point month-on-month rise, mainly due to an increase of one percentage point in interest rates on mortgage bonds following a surprise one point increase in the Bank rate to 17 percent in late November.
Transport kicked in with a 0.2 point contribution to the monthly following an eight cents per litre increase in the price of gasoline. Food contributed 0.2, tobacco products 0.1 and other items 0.1.
Within the food component there was a notable 4.3 percent monthly increase in the price of meat in the run-up to Christmas but this was partially offset by a 4.7 percent decrease in vegetable prices.
